column37: La narcolepsie est un trouble du sommeil caracterise par de la somnolence diurne excessive. Il en existe deux types : la narcolepsie de type-1 et la narcolepsie de type-2. La narcolepsie de type-1 se caracterise par un symptome particulier?: la cataplexie, soit des pertes soudaines de tonus musculaire pendant l'eveil. La cataplexie serait causee par une deficience en hypocretine, un neurotransmetteur implique dans la regulation de l'eveil et du sommeil. Les patients narcoleptiques des deux types rapportent souvent un sommeil mouvemente et non reparateur, qui s'expliquerait entre autres par l'architecture anormale de leur sommeil. Chez ces patients, on observe egalement des symptomes depressifs importants. Dans la narcolepsie de type-1, ces derniers sont souvent associes a leur deficience en hypocretine, ce qui n'est pas le cas pour la narcolepsie de type-2. Des etudes ont demontre qu'une privation de sommeil augmente les symptomes de troubles de l'humeur. Ainsi, puisque le sommeil joue un role important dans la regulation de l'humeur, nous faisons l'hypothese que des anomalies plus importantes du sommeil, particulierement la fragmentation du sommeil et une courte duree de sommeil paradoxal, seront associees a une symptomatologie depressive plus importante. Nous predisons egalement qu'une association plus importante sera observee entre l'architecture du sommeil et les symptomes depressifs dans le groupe de narcoleptiques de type-2 etant donne que l'etiologie des symptomes depressifs sera plus specifique aux alterations du sommeil.

column36: Therapeutic Potential of TG2 Inhibitors as Modulators of the Ovarian Cancer Microenvironment
column37: Ovarian cancer is the most lethal gynecological cancer worldwide and has a 5-year survival rate of less than 40%. Women are usually diagnosed after their cancer has grown large and/or spread throughout the body. Many of these cancers will develop resistance to chemotherapy and stop responding to treatment, emphasizing the need for improved treatments. Recent studies have shown that components of the environment surrounding cancer cells, namely immune cells and structural proteins, play a key role in determining how quickly a cancer will grow, metastasize and whether or not it will respond to chemotherapy. Macrophages, a type of immune cell, are the most common immune cells found around ovarian cancer cells. When present in tumours, these cells help cancer cells evade immune detection and promote changes in structural proteins that can make cancer cells more drug resistant and motile. We plan to study how ovarian cancer cells change macrophage function and how this change impacts the structural matrix surrounding ovarian cancer. To study this, we will be focusing on how tissue transglutaminase (TG2) is involved in this process. TG2 is a protein with several functions; it is expressed in macrophages and is involved in structural protein remodeling. Furthermore, this protein promotes cancer cell migration and is associated with poor patient survival. We propose that loss of TG2 activity will prevent the remodeling process by inhibiting the macrophages. We will also examine whether new TG2 inhibitors can increase the ability of macrophages to target cancer cells and prevent tissue remodeling, leading to reduced cancer spread and increased survival in mice.

column37: Many substance use disorder (SUD) programs do not integrate treatment for mental illnesses, which leads to worse outcomes for the patients. column36: Investigation of endoplasmic reticulum calcium signaling in striatal neurons of the YAC128 Huntington's disease mouse model
column37: Huntingtons disease (HD) is a neurodegenerative disorder characterized by loss of motor control, involuntary movement and cognitive deficits. HD results from a mutation on the Huntingtin gene (HTT) and involves disrupted signaling within the striatum, a brain region important for motor learning. While there is currently no cure for HD, some studies have identified Ca2+ signaling as a potential target for therapeutic intervention, as neurons depend on controlled Ca2+ homeostasis to regulate synaptic transmission. column37: In the heart, KCNQ1 (Q1) is a potassium pore which associates with the regulatory subunit KCNE1 to form the I ion channel complex. column37: Soft tissue sarcomas (STS) are rare cancers that come from muscles, fat, and cartilage. Half of all patients have metastases, which are tumours that grow in another part of the body. To determine this, I will first stain archived tissues from both sites with probes for specific proteins. I plan to detect proteins from each type of WBCs with an in-depth look at types known to help tumour growth in other cancers. These probes will tell us what WBC types are present and the number of each type will be used for comparison between the two tissues. We will then extract RNA from these tissues and use computer programs to find what type of WBCs are present and compare genetic traits between the two tissues. To confirm our data, tissues collected after surgery will be stained with similar probes from the archived tissues but use a precise laser-based method. Knowing the WBCs present in the lung metastases will ultimately help develop better immunotherapies which could cure patients with metastatic STS.

column36: Modulating Cortical Excitability of the Bilateral Representation of the Tibialis Anterior Muscle
column37: The primary motor cortex (M1) is a brain region responsible for controlling fine walking movements. In certain neurological conditions, excitability of M1 is reduced leading to gait deficits. With non-invasive brain stimulation techniques like transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS), we can assess and modulate M1 excitability by targeting muscles used in walking. For instance, tibialis anterior (TA) is a muscle recruited in the swing phase of gait. Its M1 representation is located deep in the brain and close to its contralateral representation. Thus, the magnetic field induced by TMS needs to be applied with specialized coils allowing for deeper stimulation. These coils are less focal leading to the stimulation of surrounding structures including the contralateral TA representation, thus affecting precision. Finding a bilateral TA representation on M1 that would elicit measurable cortical and muscular responses on both the left and right TA would give more control over the stimulation and would be a promising intervention that could be added to current gait rehabilitation programs. Therefore, the aim of this study is to evaluate the feasibility and efficacy of TMS over a bilateral TA representation on M1. To evaluate M1 excitability, responses in both TA muscles will be recorded with electromyography. The positions eliciting the largest TA muscular responses will be marked as the left, right, and bilateral hotspots. Brain excitability will be measured pre- and post-TMS by looking at the TA responses. There will be 3 TMS sessions to assess outcomes of continuous, intermittent, and sham stimulation based on the muscular responses. Bilateral hotspot stimulation and effects of the 3 sessions on cortical excitability will be analyzed with a two-way repeated measures ANOVA.

column36: Examining Links between General Fatigue in Myasthenia Gravis with Objectively Measured Sleep
column37: Myasthenia Gravis and SleepMyasthenia gravis (MG) is an autoimmune disease that affects a patients nervous system, as the patients own immune system creates antibodies that attack nerve endings at their connection points to the muscle. Although muscle weakness is a hallmark symptom of MG, many patients also report symptoms of general fatigue, which is defined as a loss of energy physically or cognitively. This can negatively impact activities of daily living and quality of life. Research in the past has shown an association between sleep disorders and general fatigue in other neurological conditions, but this relationship has rarely been explored in MG patients. Furthermore, while some research studies in the past have found a correlation between MG and higher prevalence of sleep disorders, other studies have not. More research is needed to fill this knowledge gap in the current literature. Since sleep disorders are readily treatable, examining their relationship with MG can potentially lead to new clinical recommendations for this patient population to help improve their symptoms and quality of life. MG patients and healthy patients will be identified at the 3 recruiting centres ; Sunnybrook Health Sciences Centre, University Health Network, and St Michaels Hospital. Participant contact information will be sent to a research coordinator at Sunnybrook who will mail out the sleep questionnaires and equipment (i.e. home sleep apnea test, actigraphy, and an Android phone that will operate the psychomotor vigilance test), and arrange for all items to be mailed back. The study will examine obstructive sleep apnea and sleep quality in MG patients, and their relationship with general fatigue.

column36: The Effects of an Exercise Program on the Metabolomic Profiles of Anthracycline-Induced Cardiotoxicity in Breast Cancer Survivors
column37: In Canada, breast cancer is the most common form of cancer. Thankfully, with evolving diagnostic technologies over the past century, the survival rate for breast cancer is 89%. Unfortunately, this increase in survivorship has allowed for the latent side-effects of cancer therapies to become apparent. One effective chemotherapy known to have toxic effects on our hearts is anthracyclines. Frequently, the heart damage is undiagnosed until significant damage occurs because the current detection methods are not strong enough. However, research in animal models suggests that heart damage may be detected by tracking changes in the molecules involved in metabolism- a field called metabolomics.Additionally, no drug can prevent heart damage caused by anthracyclines. However, the current research suggests that exercise may be an effective treatment. Exercise's effectiveness may be detected by changes in the metabolomics of heart cells. As such, the purpose of this research project is to see if a 24-week exercise intervention improves the heart health of cancer survivors receiving anthracyclines by looking at metabolomic profiles. A standard of care control group and an exercise intervention group will be randomly formed from a sample of pre-treatment adult breast cancer survivors. The exercise group will then complete a 24-week aerobic-based exercise program. At the same time, the standard of care group will continue with their day-to-day lives. This research, if proven statistically, would offer evidence to support the mitigating effect that exercise provides on heart damage caused by anthracyclines and how metabolomic profiles of heart cells are impacted by exercise. Such results would support the implementation of exercise programs for patients receiving anthracyclines.

column36: Improving the Response of the Ovarian Tumour Microenvironment to PARP Inhibitors
column37: Ovarian cancer is the most lethal gynecological cancer and has a 5-year survival rate of less than 45%. About 20% of patients with high-grade serous ovarian cancer have mutations in the genes. These genes code for the proteins in one of the main DNA repair pathways, known as homologous recombination. As such, the mutated cells become reliant on other DNA repair pathways, such as the poly-adenosine diphosphate-ribose polymerase (PARP) repair mechanisms. This causes these cells to become sensitive to a family of drugs known as PARP inhibitors (PARPi), which are now commonly used as maintenance therapy. Although PARPi have been very beneficial to patients, the PARPi induced response of the tissue surrounding the cancer cells, known as the tumour microenvironment (TME), remains unknown. Therefore, this project aims to study the changes in the ovarian TME following the administration of PARPi. To do this, we will induce the development of ovarian cancer in mice over 30 days and then administer PARPi for a total of 18 days. Thereafter, the tumours will be collected from the mice and analyzed for expression of markers of cell growth, inflammation, and cell death. Additionally, we will use flow cytometry, a technique that allows us to establish the immune cell composition of the TME. Because the TME is often highly immunosuppressive and is composed of anti-inflammatory cell types, we hypothesize that by learning the response of the TME to PARPi treatment, we can identify ways to manipulate the TME to boost the immune response. In the longer term, the outcomes of this study will be used to design more effective combination therapies to treat ovarian cancer and prolong patient survival.

column36: Assessing Feasibility of a Novel Full Head Coverage Functional Near Infrared Spectroscopy Device to Monitor Perioperative Stroke Development During Cardiac Surgery
column37: Perioperative stroke (PS) is one of the most severe and devastating complications of heart surgery. PS is when blood supply to part of the brain is impaired either during or shortly after surgery. This can have serious effects on a patient as it means that part of the brain is not receiving sufficient oxygen, which can quickly lead to tissue damage, leaving patients with major disabilities. Monitoring how much oxygen each area of the brain is receiving would help surgeons identify a problem early and intervene when possible. The most common method currently used for brain monitoring during surgery is cerebral oximetry which uses light to measure tissue oxygenation. However, current oximeters can only monitor brain oxygenation in the forehead, meaning possible oxygen disruptions to other regions will go undetected. Recent technology developments have led to a new optical device called Kernel Flow that has the capability to monitor regional tissue oxygenation across the entire head. My project has two aims: First to assess how well the Kernel Flow system can detect regional brain oxygenation changes in healthy volunteers. Second, to evaluate the feasibility of using the Kernel Flow for brain monitoring during heart surgery. The results of these aims will highlight the promise of this technology for reducing the incidence of perioperative stroke, ultimately leading to improved patient outcomes.

column36: Mobile App-Delivered Motivational Interviewing for Individuals on an Eating Disorder Clinic Waitlist: Pilot and Feasibility Study
column37: Eating disorders (EDs) are life-threatening mental illnesses with serious health consequences. Despite having the highest mortality rate of any mental disorder, individuals with EDs are far less likely to access treatment compared to those with other mental health problems due to various barriers (e.g., long wait-lists, scarcity of treatment centres, low motivation for change, high rates of treatment dropout). The COVID-19 pandemic has further exacerbated these issues, with reports of increased rates of EDs, longer wait-times, and decreased motivation for ED recovery. Motivational interviewing (MI) is a psychological intervention method that is effective in addressing many of the treatment issues associated with EDs including resistance to change and treatment dropout. Furthermore, brief MI interventions, administered prior to the onset of formal ED treatment, have been shown to improve overall clinical outcomes. Mobile-phone apps have been suggested as a cost-effective way to deliver such interventions. Despite their potential, there have yet to be any studies examining app-based MI to target EDs. The following proposal aims to pilot test and examine the feasibility and acceptability of MI-Coach, a widely-available MI mobile app, for individuals on waitlists for ED treatment. Measures of clinical profiles, ED severity, and motivation for change will be examined before and after a one-month use of MI-Coach. In addition, participants perceptions of the apps ease of use, perceived usefulness, and quality will be examined. This study has the potential to transform ED service delivery while simultaneously providing tangible psychological support to its participants.

column36: Evaluating a precision medicine approach to nephrotic syndrome using novel genetic risk profiles: A pilot adaptive clinical trial
column37: Nephrotic syndrome is one of the most common childhood kidney diseases. It is diagnosed in up to 3,000 Canadian children each year. In nephrotic syndrome, the kidneys leak protein into the urine, which decreases the amount of protein in the blood, and causes swelling of the body. This can cause breathing problems, infections, and blood clots. The cause of nephrotic syndrome is unknown, but we think that genetic differences and the immune system are involved. Most children respond to steroid treatment, but many have frequent disease relapses. These children receive lots of steroids and other medications to suppress the immune system. These have many side effects, and every child responds differently to treatment. We still dont know what the best medications are to treat nephrotic syndrome. And we dont have tools to predict which children will respond to medications. Creating these tools could reduce the number of medications tried, prevent side effects, and get children to respond to treatment sooner.Using genetic information from over 750 children with and without nephrotic syndrome, we are creating a prediction tool to identify which children will develop severe disease and which will respond to different treatments. The goal of this research is to learn whether using this genetic prediction tool to make treatment decisions is better than current treatment without the tool. To do so, we will first perform a ;pilot study in a small number of children with nephrotic syndrome in Toronto, to ensure that our research is feasible and safe. If this genetic prediction tool is effective, it will allow doctors to use a ;precision medicine approach to treat childhood nephrotic syndrome. This can improve the care of these children and reduce disease complications.

column36: We were always here: adapting virtual care for Chinese Canadian prostate cancer survivors
column37: We were always here - adapting virtual care for Chinese Canadian prostate cancer survivorsProstate cancer (PCa) is the most commonly diagnosed cancer in Canadian men. 1 in 8 men in Canada will be diagnosed with PCa, and 91% will survive at least 5 years beyond diagnosis. These survivors often have bodily impairments and post-treatment challenges. Current follow-up care protocols schedule patients to visit their oncologist every few months, which can make it difficult to manage these challenges. These protocols are not easily scalable and are also not often adapted for cultural contexts. Virtual care can help relieve these pressures. However, equitable implementation of virtual care must include and understand the needs of marginalized communities. My research aims to bridge the divide by adapting virtual prostate cancer follow-up care for Chinese Canadian men in partnership with this community. Chinese Canadians are one of the largest visible minority groups in Canada, and approximately 70% identify as first generation. As the project lead, I will interview Chinese Canadian PCa survivors to understand the common themes among their experiences and create user recommendations to develop an adaptation of Ned. Ned is an innovative prostate cancer virtual care application and clinic developed with patients and providers at University Health Network. This adaptation will be iteratively reviewed and refined together with these survivors. The final result will be a greater understanding of the experience of Chinese Canadian men with prostate cancer and a validated Ned blueprint that serves the specific follow-up care needs of this group. Ultimately, it will be a model for cultural adaptations of virtual care for cancer survivorship, increasing access for all.

column37: Obesity associated type 2 diabetes is characterized by a disruption in glucose homeostasis and energy balance in males and females. column36: Quand le virtuel interfere avec le reel
column37: Ce projet de recherche a pour objectif d'explorer l'effet d'un type de reseaux sociaux (Instagram) sur les perturbations de l'image corporelle aupres de populations presentant des attitudes et comportements alimentaires dysfonctionnels (ACAD). La pertinence du developpement de ce projet reside dans l'observation d'une augmentation de l'utilisation problematique d'internet et des reseaux sociaux en temps de COVID-19 et a ses impacts sur la sante mentale des utilisateurs (Fernandes, 2020). Le contenu partage sur les medias de masse, demontrant souvent des ideaux de beaute irrealistes, serait un facteur causant une augmentation de la prevalence d'individu ayant une image du corps negative et augmenterait le desir d'atteindre un certain type de corps idealise par la societe (Lwin & Malik, 2012). En effet, les medias sociaux, comme Instagram, sont souvent percus comme etant un facteur de risque, car ceux-ci sont orientes vers les commentaires sur l'apparence physique ce qui a pour effet d'augmenter l'insatisfaction corporelle (Griffiths et al., 2018?; Sidanie et al., 2016?; Tiggeman et Barbato, 2018).Dans cette etude, ce lien entre l'utilisation des reseaux sociaux et les perturbations de l'image corporelle sera etudie chez une population presentant une ACAD, cette derniere etant plus susceptible de developper un trouble du comportement alimentaire (TCA). En effet, les ACAD entrainent d'importantes consequences sur le plan individuel et psychologique et sont reconnus comme des precurseurs des TCA (Labossiere, 2019; Turgeon et al, 2015). A ce jour, seulement quelques etudes empiriques ont documente l'influence des reseaux sociaux sur les perturbations de l'image corporelle, et aucune, a notre connaissance, n'a documente ce lien chez une population presentant une ACAD.

column36: Sleep Disordered Breathing and Cerebral Small Vessel Disease in the Cognitively Impaired: A Useful Therapeutic Target?
column37: Sleep disordered breathing is common in aging and contributes negatively to both cardiovascular and brain health outcomes. A common form of sleep disordered breathing, obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), is characterized by repetitive upper airway collapse during sleep causing reduced airflow, which results in reduced blood oxygen concentration. Patients may experience excessive daytime sleepiness, which can be debilitating and impair daytime functioning. OSA has been linked to cerebral small vessel disease (SVD), which is visible on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) brain scans, as well as declining cognitive function. Additionally, a common treatment for OSA, continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP), effectively reduces the symptoms of OSA and slows cognitive impairment. However, the majority of prior work has explored individuals with normal cognitive function, and almost none of the past research has focused on patients with varying degrees of cognitive impairment.The research proposed here aims to determine if OSA is linked to SVD in cognitively impaired people. Additionally, it aims to discover if SVD impacts the effectiveness of CPAP on cognitive function in the cognitively impaired. The subjects for this study will be patients diagnosed with cognitive impairment at Sunnybrook Health Sciences Centre. All subjects will undergo sleep testing, an MRI scan, and cognitive testing. MRI scans will be processed using an imaging pipeline to determine the severity of SVD in patients. Currently, there are no effective methods for stopping or reversing cognitive impairment in patients with dementia and Alzheimers disease. The research proposed here may reveal whether OSA is a therapeutic target for preserving or improving cognitive function in these patients.

column36: Understanding the implication of germline missense variants in DICER1 syndrome
column37: DICER1 syndrome is a genetic disease that predisposes affected individuals to developing multiple tumours in different organs during childhood, notably in the lungs, thyroid, and kidneys. The disease is caused by two variants in the DICER1 gene. The first is generally inherited from one parent or newly found in an individual. The second variant is then spontaneously acquired in a cell of an organ, which leads to a tumour forming. In order to better understand how certain DICER1 variants can cause this disease, we will focus on the first variant that predisposes individuals to this syndrome. Most of the time, this variant causes a complete loss of the function of the gene. Interestingly, there is a group of patients in which this initial variant does not cause a complete loss of function of the gene, also known as a missense variant. My project focuses on determining the effect of such variants on the function of the DICER1 gene. This will allow a better understanding of the disease and provide valuable information for clinicians to understand which variants are implicated in DICER1 syndrome.

column36: Role of Adamts19 in Heart Valve Disease
column37: Heart valves are crucial in maintaining the unidirectional flow of blood through the heart. These form early during development of the embryo and continue to mature throughout development and after birth. Heart valves have a distinct three-layered tissue structure that corresponds to their specialized function. In cases where valves do not properly develop, they can become malformed leading to disease and requiring medical treatment. Currently, end-stage valve disease and very early valve formation is well known however, there is more research needed to understand fetal and postanal valve development. Previous work in the Andelfinger lab has identified that the gene Adamts19, when missing, can lead to diseased valves without their stereotypical structure. It is thought that Adamts19 is required to rearrange cells into their normal layers however, it is unclear how this gene communicates to cells to form healthy valves. My project aims to investigate how valves develop in mice lacking the Adamts19 gene and identify how Adamts19 can cause molecular and cellular changes that lead to valve disease. Hopefully, this work will improve the understanding of how valves mature and to provide more effective therapeutics.

column36: Bonification du protocole neuropsychologique utilise aupres des patients presentant une hydrocephalie a pression normale
column37: L'hydrocephalie a pression normale est un trouble neurologique caracterise par des troubles de la marche, une incontinence urinaire et des troubles cognitifs. Un traitement chirurgical s'avere toutefois efficace pour reduire ces symptomes. Neanmoins, ce traitement implique une chirurgie dans le cerveau. Il devient donc crucial d'identifier les patients susceptibles d'y repondre positivement. Pour ce faire, une ponction lombaire, qui consiste a retirer du liquide cephalorachidien se situant dans le dos, est realisee. Cette ponction lombaire permet de simuler l'effet qu'aurait la chirurgie chez le patient. Si une amelioration significative des symptomes cognitifs et de la marche s'observe apres cette simulation, le patient est refere pour la chirurgie. Or, les tests actuellement utilises pour evaluer l'amelioration des symptomes cognitifs ne sont pas assez sensibles, ce qui empeche plusieurs patients de beneficier du traitement. Pour remedier a cette lacune, il devient essentiel d'identifier des tests cognitifs ayant une meilleure sensibilite. A cet effet, il est rapporte que le Line tracing test et le Serial dotting test, deux tests cognitifs, permettraient de detecter ces ameliorations. Cependant, en raison du manque d'etudes appreciant leur sensibilite pour deceler un changement a la suite d'une ponction lombaire, ces evaluations sont peu utilisees en clinique. Le present projet vise donc a evaluer si le Line tracing test et le Serial dotting test permettent de detecter des ameliorations cognitives chez les patients ayant effectue une ponction lombaire. Les retombees de ce projet permettront aux neuropsychologues de disposer d'evaluations plus sensibles pour identifier les patients eligibles a la chirurgie. Cela ameliorera donc la qualite de vie de plusieurs patients.

column36: Epidemiological risk model to inform targeted prevention strategies in endometrial cancer
column37: The proposed research project focuses on validating an epidemiological risk model to improve targeted prevention strategies for endometrial cancer (EC), or cancer of the uterus. This gynaecological cancer is an epidemic with rising incidence and mortality rates. EC treatment involves surgical hysterectomies, or uterus removal, as chemotherapeutic strategies are lacking; however, data reveals that 15-20% of EC patients have recurring cancer prior to hysterectomies. Clinicians should focus on assessing endometrial hyperplasia (EH), a precursor of EC with similar risk factors and a more common diagnosis. Early detection of EH is proactive as it is 80-100% reversible. Our research aims to validate and improve two pre-existing risk models for EC that show early predicting ability but lack consistent validation. These models utilize data from the Canada Partnership for Tomorrow Project (CanPath), a large prospective cohort study focusing on cancer prevention. Validation will be done by considering commonly associated risk factors and improving such models by including additional factors from baseline CanPath data such as EH incidence, and gender and socio-ethnical impacts. Once validated, the two previously proposed risk models for EC will allow stratification of at-risk patients to appropriate prevention strategies. Risk model improvement is critical as EC risk factors are modifiable; this may enhance tailored prevention strategies, allowing for identification of high-risk asymptomatic women. This investigation is also beneficial for addressing inequities associated with cancer by assessing how gender and socio-ethnical constructs fit into our EC risk models which allows screening to impact a wider audience. Ultimately, our goal is to potentially reduce EC incidence by 80%.

column36: Identification of disease-associated immune cells and inflammatory cytokines in a MATR3 S85C knock-in mouse model of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis
column37: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is a neurodegenerative disease that involves the gradual loss of motor neurons, leading to paralysis and death. Although the cause of ALS is unknown, neuroinflammation has been proposed as a possible mechanism leading to ALS. Microglial cells that are part of the innate immune system were found to be significantly increased in the central nervous system (CNS) of ALS patients and mice models. However, inflammation is not limited to these cells as dysregulation of peripheral adaptive immune cells, including B and T cells, may cause a systematic inflammatory response that affects the CNS. However, there is limited data on the role of the adaptive immune system in ALS.Recently, our lab generated a mouse model which recapitulates key features of early-stage ALS including neuromuscular junction defects and motor deficits. Interestingly, I found an increased number of B cells and an upregulation of inflammatory genes in the brains of the mutant mice, supporting the idea that the adaptive immune system may play a critical role in ALS. To further study the role of this system, I will quantify the blood cell populations and examine if they infiltrate skeletal muscle tissues affected in ALS. Additionally, as immune cells release signalling molecules called cytokines, I will determine if the levels of cytokines differ between the mutant and wildtype mice. I hypothesize that a specific combination of immune cells and cytokines will be associated with disease progression, acting as potential biomarkers for ALS. Thus, identification of these specific and sensitive biomarkers could be used to diagnose ALS at an early stage and enable the development of early therapeutic intervention strategies.

column36: Quand l'intelligence autistique s'exerce sans contraintes : l'apprentissage et les mecanismes du calcul de calendrier dans l'autisme
column37: Le syndrome du savant se caracterise par des habiletes exceptionnelles contrastant avec un fonctionnement cognitif et/ou adaptatif plus faible (Bolte et Poustka, 2004). Sa prevalence se situe autour de 0,06 %. Pres de 75 % des individus savants appartiennent au spectre autistique. Les etudes de cas de syndrome rares ont ete decisives en neuropsychologie (Ogden, 2005). Dans l'autisme, des etudes de cas approfondies de savants (Mottron et Belleville, 1993) ont mis a jour des mecanismes qui, une fois repliques dans l'autisme non savant, ont permis d'avancer la comprehension des specificites cognitives autistiques. Le calcul de calendrier est l'habilete la plus frequente. Il consiste en la capacite de completer (en general, en quelques secondes) une information portant sur les calendriers, comme la question : << quel jour de la semaine etions-nous le 12 septembre 1978? >>. Des hypotheses sur les processus cognitifs impliques dans cette habilete ont ete proposees a partir des etudes de cas (Cowan et al., 2001). Aucun consensus n'existe sur le ou les procedes utilises par les calculateurs de calendrier. L'objectif principal du present projet est de mieux documenter les processus cognitifs impliques dans l'habilete exceptionnelle de calcul de calendrier autiste. Nous conduirons d'abord une revue systematique de la litterature des etudes de cas disponibles sur le sujet. A partir des resultats sur les modeles proposes et les secteurs qui n'ont pas fait l'objet d'une exploration scientifique, nous effectuerons des etudes de cas multiples. Ce projet offrira une meilleure comprehension du fonctionnement cognitif en autisme par le biais du calcul de calendrier. Ces connaissances permettront de travailler les forces de ces personnes et d'agrementer les pratiques educatives.

column36: The Cognitive Kitchen: A Virtual Culinary Intervention for Dementia Prevention
column37: Primary prevention efforts to reduce the risk of dementia have become a public health priority, given the absence of cure and paucity of treatment options. Approximately one-third of dementia diagnoses are attributed to modifiable risk factors, and nutrition is a key modifiable factor. As such, promotion of nutrition strategies that have a neuroprotective effect or delay cognitive impairment are a priority. While the link between nutrition and cognitive function involves several factors, culinary and nutrition education interventions (sometimes called community kitchens) provide a suitable environment to expand awareness of modifiable risk factors for dementia and support positive lifestyle behaviours. Virtually-delivered community kitchens have not been widely investigated and have potential to increase the reach of programs to rural and remote areas. We are developing The Cognitive Kitchen to fulfill this opportunity. The aim of this study is to deliver a 6-week virtual culinary intervention designed to reduce risk factors for dementia and explore the experiences of community-dwelling older adult participants. Objectives include: 1) Implement a virtual nutrition intervention to translate the principles of evidence-based eating patterns and practices to prevent dementia; 2) Determine the feasibility and acceptability of the program to a diverse sample (age, gender, SES, ethnicity) of community-dwelling older adult participants; 3) Increase participants enjoyment of and confidence in cooking skills and healthy eating to promote it as a meaningful daily activity that contributes to well-being; 4) Test the use of validated instruments to examine changes in nutrition knowledge and food agency, and quality of life among participants post-intervention.

column36: Senescence et resistance a la therapie en cancer de l'ovaire
column37: La therapie contre le cancer peut rendre nos cellules senescentes, un etat qui signifie l'arret de leur multiplication. En cancer, les cellules se divisent de facon incontrolee : la senescence peut etre benefique en ralentissant leur progression. Toutefois, il a ete trouve que cette senescence a aussi des effets contraires favorisant la progression du cancer par d'autres mecanismes. Ainsi, une nouvelle strategie consiste a rendre les cellules cancereuses senescentes pour stopper leur progression, puis a les detruire avec des medicaments specifiques pour eviter les effets nefastes.Cependant, meme avec cette strategie, il y a de la resistance a la therapie, car les cellules senescentes sont tres differentes l'une de l'autre. Nous pensons que de trouver une signature des cellules senescentes aiderait a leur elimination avec des medicaments specifiques, pour combattre plus efficacement le cancer.Pour etudier cette signature, nous utiliserons des cellules de cancer de l'ovaire a cellules claires. Il s'agit d'un type de cancer de l'ovaire qui resiste a tous les traitements presentement. C'est un bon modele : nous avons confirme que la senescence est tres differente d'une cellule a l'autre apres la therapie, ce qui rend difficile son elimination par les medicaments. Normalement, les analyses sont effectuees sur toute la population de cellules, ce qui ne represente pas bien leurs differences. Nous allons plutot utiliser une approche unicellulaire, donc une analyse precise de chaque cellule, pour observer les disparites et decouvrir de nouvelles cibles pour les medicaments.Cette etude nous permettra de comprendre la resistance a la therapie pour le cancer de l'ovaire a cellule claire, et qui sait, peut-etre un jour celle de tous les cancers!

column36: Investigating the Effects of Cannabis on Adolescent Rodent Brains using Vapour Chambers and Magnetic Resonance Imaging
column37: The proposed research project will investigate the effects of cannabis consumption on adolescent rat brains. These rats will be exposed to cannabis using vapour chambers, which are essentially enclosed boxes that the rats will be placed in. Once in these boxes, cannabis will be vaporized, the vapour will enter the box, and the rat will inhale the cannabis vapour. The dosage will be controlled so that the blood-THC levels of the rats are comparable to those seen in humans consuming cannabis. Given that inhaling vaporized cannabis is a common route of cannabis administration in humans, particularly in youth, this method of administration also makes the rodent research more translational to humans. Following cannabis exposure, the rodents will be assessed for differences in behaviour using navigational tasks and altered neural structure using magnetic resonance imaging (MRI).The frequency of exposure will vary to reflect cannabis-use patterns in humans. The rats will be divided into four groups: 1) a control group that is not exposed to cannabis; 2) an infrequent user group that will rarely be exposed to cannabis; 3) a frequent user group that does not escalate in the amount used; 4) and a frequent user group that escalates the amount of cannabis used over time. The four groups will then be compared to look for structural and behavioural differences. This is relevant because, since cannabis has been legalized in Canada, the impacts of cannabis use on the developing adolescent brain have been of high interest in health research. However, previous rodent research lacks control in utilizing dosages, frequency, and administrative routes that are typical of human use. The current methodology aims to control for this and produce sound data on youth-cannabis consumption.

column36: A Pilot Intervention for Illness Uncertainty and Intolerance of Uncertainty in Comorbid Anxiety and Depression in Rheumatoid Arthritis
column37: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a debilitating autoimmune disease characterized by chronic inflammation that can lead to permanent physical damage and hinder the psychological wellbeing across the lifespan. Adjustment to life with RA involves a significant amount of coping with the unpredictable nature of the disease. RA coupled with the co-occurrence of anxiety or depression raises concern for this population as they are already at increased risk for poorer physical health and have limited access to support. The uncertainty from RA when paired with the inability to tolerate uncertainty stemming from emotional disorders can lead to increased pain, more severe symptoms across conditions, poorer quality of life, and less likelihood of following treatment plans. Of utmost concern, is whether diagnosed patients with comorbid anxiety or depressive disorders in RA are adequately equipped with coping skills to handle the volume of unforeseen and uncontrollable change. The proposed project will be the first to implement and evaluate a modified cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT) intervention for co-occurring emotional disorders in RA targeting illness uncertainty and intolerance of uncertainty. The proposed trial of an uncertainty-focused CBT intervention will help promote overall quality life and reduce symptoms across conditions. Findings from the measurement of treatment outcomes before and after participating in the program will be beneficial for encouraging greater inclusion of mental health screening in those with RA. Additional support will be garnered advocating for the use of a multidisciplinary approach for care to reduce anxiety, depression, and RA severity in turn contributing to improvement in overall quality of life.

column36: Preschool Diet and Child Health Outcomes: The CHILD Cohort Study
column37: Epidemiological evidence suggests that nutrition in early life may play an important role for the susceptibility to develop chronic disease in later life. While there is extensive research around diet and adult health, the research into the impact of diet on the health of preschool children is lacking. Therefore, my research aim is to determine the association between diet in preschool aged children and health outcomes, employing longitudinal data from the largest cross-Canadian birth cohort study to date, the CHILD Cohort Study. To achieve this aim, food frequency questionnaires, previously obtained from 5-year-old children participating in the CHILD cohort study, and their uniquely-derived dietary patterns, will be validated using two approaches; anthropometrics and metabolomics. Then, the prevalence of cardiometabolic health outcomes and asthma in the different dietary patterns will be studied and compared. These scientific findings will help further inform dietary recommendations for Canadian children and help clinicians suggest dietary adjustments for at risk populations, to decrease disease prevalence and increase positive health outcomes in Canadian children.

column36: Consommation d'aliments ultra-transformes chez les communautes ethnoculturelles et les nouveaux arrivants au Canada
column37: En general, les immigrants sont en meilleure sante que les Canadiens lors de leur arrivee au pays, mais celle-ci se deteriore avec le temps. Ceci est du en partie a la transition dans les habitudes alimentaires, entres autres avec une augmentation de la consommation d'aliments ultra-transformes (AUT). Cette augmentation est preoccupante etant donne que la consommation de ces produits augmente le risque d'obesite, de plusieurs maladies chroniques et de mortalite. Or, les niveaux de consommation des AUT, ainsi que les defis et les experiences en lien avec ceux-ci au sein des diverses communautes immigrantes au Canada ne sont pas encore bien connus. Ce projet propose donc de mieux comprendre la transition nutritionnelle des immigrants a travers la consommation d'AUT et d'identifier les differents facteurs qui predisposent, permettent et renforcent l'acculturation alimentaire au sein de communautes culturelles canadienne. Pour cette etude, la consommation de produits ultra-transformes sera d'abord estime en utilisant l'enquete de sante dans les collectivites canadiennes de 2015 en fonction de l'appartenance ethnoculturelle et le statut migratoire. Dans un deuxieme temps, des groupes de discussion seront effectues aupres de membres issus des groupes ethnoculturels cibles afin de mieux comprendre les donnees presentees dans la premiere phase en questionnant les participants sur leur connaissances, perceptions et experiences en lien avec la consommation d'AUT. Comprendre les causes de l'acculturation alimentaire de certaines populations immigrantes aidera a davantage cibler les interventions aupres des nouveaux arrivants afin de reduire l'apport des AUT et de prevenir ce faisant le developpement de maladies chroniques chez ces communautes.

column36: Exploring the effects of manipulating the transcriptional regulatory networks of tissue-resident lung macrophage populations in mouse models of pulmonary fibrosis
column37: Interstitial lung disease (ILD) is a broad term referring to several diseases causing lung fibrosis, which increases lung stiffness, making it harder to breathe. Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is one of the most common ILDs and has devastating implications. It is a chronic progressive lung disease, with a median survival of 3-5 years. The available drug therapies for IPF are poorly understood and ineffective, having only the ability to slow down disease progression. This means that an IPF diagnosis is often equivalent to a slow and painful death. Tissue-resident macrophages, one of the innate immune cell populations in the lung, are thought to play a role in the development of IPF. These cells are important for tasks such as the detection and destruction of harmful organisms and the initiation of local inflammation. Previous work has shown that elimination of lung macrophages prevented the onset of fibrosis in mice. This is not feasible in humans with IPF, and would cause increased susceptibility to infection. We will explore the transcriptional regulatory networks (TRNs) of macrophage populations within fibrotic and non-fibrotic lungs. To do this, transcriptional and genomics data will be collected from mouse models of fibrosis. This information will be used to select gene targets, which we will knockout in lung macrophages. Using bioinformatics techniques, we will compare the effects of these knockouts on fibrosis. A reduction in fibrosis will indicate the knockout gene was positively influencing the macrophage response in the fibrotic phenotype. This will help us to better understand the interactions macrophages have with their environment and their role in the promotion of fibrosis, and could lead to potential new IPF targets.

column36: Evaluating Insulin-like Growth Factor-Binding Protein 3 (IGFBP3) as a novel drug target in Head and Neck Cancer
column37: Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma (HNSCC) is one of the deadliest and most prevalent cancers with rising incidence. The treatment options are non-selective and associated with toxicities and other adverse effects, thus highlighting the need for novel therapeutic strategies. CRISPR screening has been widely used to identify genetic vulnerabilities in cancer cell lines. However, these in vitro models lack the tumour microenvironment and do not fully capture the intricate biology of tumours. To address this issue, our group has established HNSCC mouse models that integrate multiplexed in vivo CRISPR/Cas9 mutagenesis to test hundreds of genes in a single mouse within a couple of weeks. To inactivate candidate cancer genes in the oral cavity and skin of mice, highly concentrated CRISPR/Cas9 lentiviruses are being delivered to the single-layer surface ectoderm of living mouse embryos via ultrasound-guided microinjections. Our first in vivo CRISPR screen, performed directly in the epithelium of tumour-prone mice, identified Insulin-like growth factor binding protein 3 (IGFBP3) as a top hit essential for the selective proliferation of transformed epithelial cells. In clinical datasets, IGFBP3 is amplified/gained in ~ 39% of HNSCC patients, and increased mRNA levels correlate with poorer survival. My project aims to combine in vivo CRISPR gene editing in mouse models of HNSCC and functional genomic experimentation in patient-derived HNSCC xenografts to further characterize the oncogenic function of IGFBP3 in HNSCC and delineate its molecular mechanism of action. Successful completion of this project will contribute to novel targeted therapeutics of HNSCC and highlight the potential of in vivo drop-out screens to detect novel, biologically relevant cancer drug targets.

column36: Impact of Traumatic Spinal Cord Injury on Work and Earnings
column37: An acute traumatic spinal cord injury (SCI) is a devastating occurrence with tremendous personal loss and societal costs. It disproportionately affects younger working-aged individuals and returning to work after such an injury is often not possible. Occupation, age, and overall health can stratify individuals into different risk categories for spinal cord injury. Many individuals experience drastic changes to their physical and mental well-being which inhibits their ability to return to a pre-injury level of work. Relatively little data is available pertaining to the labour market impacts of acute traumatic SCI. Most of the current data is derived from small survey studies on highly selected patient populations. In this study, we will utilize a national Canadian database linking inpatient hospitalization information with taxation data to estimate the impact an acute traumatic SCI has on employment and income in working aged individuals. To empirically examine the effects of traumatic SCI, we will use econometric methodology to compare pre and post injury levels of employment and income. Our study will add to the current body of knowledge by using a large sample of patients from a Canadian national linked database between healthcare information and taxation filings to objectively study the impact of this devastating traumatic injury on employment and income.

column36: Optimizing brain-computer interfaces for children: Mitigating fatigue through gamification
column37: Communicating with others, exploring the environment, and playing games are part of childhood for typically developing children. However, kids with severe neuromotor disabilities such as cerebral palsy are often unable to exercise such autonomy as they grow. Brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) offer a possible avenue by which children unable to move or speak can attain these fundamental human rights. BCIs bypass the muscular system by recording an individuals brain activity and directly transforming signals to control devices such as a wheelchair, computer, or video game. BCI research is a growing field but it often neglects pediatric populations. We aim to change that. Our team, called BCI4kids, is the worlds only patient-and family-centered clinical pediatric BCI program. We have demonstrated that both typically developing and severely disabled children can successfully operate BCIs to perform fun and meaningful tasks independently. To improve such life-changing intervention for children with neuromotor disability, we need to identify factors by which the young brains of children can achieve optimal BCI performance. Fatigue is an important factor to consider, as BCIs require sustained focus. The proposed study will specifically address the role of fatigue and how gamification of BCI applications can reduce this barrier while enhancing performance and enjoyment. We will engage a large group of typically developing children who will learn to perform multiple tasks using regular and game versions of existing BCI applications while evaluating the causes and effects of fatigue. This information will directly inform the design of pediatric and adult BCI technologies and programs for the goals identified by the severely disabled children and their families in our BCI program.

column36: Recuperation a long terme de la marche apres lesion medullaire: impact des neuroprotheses de stimulation corticale
column37: Les lesions medullaires sont la seconde cause de paralysie apres l'accident vasculaire cerebral. Le plus souvent, meme une readaptation intensive ne permet qu'une recuperation partielle de la marche. La plasticite des circuits moteurs spinaux et corticaux est essentielle a la recuperation locomotrice apres une blessure medullaire. Nous avons developpe une interface stimulant la representation de la patte posterieure du cortex moteur bilateralement, de facon synchrone avec les phases de la marche. Chez le rat blesse medullaire, la readaptation avec une stimulation pendant la marche permet une meilleure recuperation de la locomotion qu'un entrainement locomoteur seul. Pour poursuivre la demarche de translation de cette technologie chez l'humain, mon projet vise a tester la neuroprothese corticale sur un modele chat avec contusion medullaire dorsale, produisant une paraplegie qui recupere partiellement avec la readaptation, similaire a une blessure medullaire incomplete chez l'humain. Les chats recevront un impact medullaire thoracique standardise creant une paralysie et des deficits du controle des membres posterieurs. Ils recevront un entrainement locomoteur (20 min/jour pour 3 semaines), avec ou sans stimulation corticale (2 groupes de 8 chats), qui sera arrete pour 4 semaines. Hebdomadairement, nous examinerons les parametres de marche sur tapis roulant et la performance de taches de controle moteur volontaire (echelle horizontale et obstacles). Notre hypothese est que l'entrainement avec stimulation ameliorera durablement la locomotion et le controle volontaire des pattes posterieures. Cette etude est une importante evaluation preclinique d'une neuroprothese, avec un potentiel de translation clinique au benefice des patients avec blessure medullaire incomplete.

column36: Etude des troubles cognitifs durant la phase aigue d'un traumatisme craniocerebral chez une population pediatrique et de leur relation avec le devenir a long terme des patients
column37: Objectif. Un traumatisme craniocerebral (TCC), lorsque subit en enfance, entraine des difficultes cognitives pouvant affecter le rendement academique, la capacite d'adaptation et la qualite de vie des enfants jusqu'a l'age adulte. Ces problemes touchent surtout l'attention, de la memoire et les fonctions executives, selon les etudes qui ont toutefois ete majoritairement realisees pendant la phase chronique du TCC. Peu d'etudes ont precise la nature des troubles cognitifs pendant la phase aigue du TCC, soit les trois premiers mois post-accident. Pourtant, l'ensemble des sequelles cognitives observees en phase aigue est le meilleur predicteur du devenir a long-terme. L'objectif de cette etude est de documenter la nature et l'intensite des sequelles cognitives des enfants et adolescents pendant la phase aigue du TCC (leger, modere, severe) a l'aide d'un test neuropsychologique exhaustif et de verifier si ces derniers predisent leur qualite de vie a plus long terme.Participants et methodes. 75 jeunes ages entre 7 et 15 ans, hospitalise au CHU de Sherbrooke et CHU Sainte-Justine pour un TCC leger a severe survenu il y a moins de 3 mois seront recrutes pour participer a l'etude. Les participants effectueront la version pediatrique de l'EXAmen cognitif abrege en Traumatologie (EXACT-P), un outil d'evaluation neuropsychologique bref evaluant le fonctionnement cognitif global durant la phase aigue du TCC. L'Inventaire de la qualite de vie pediatrique leur sera egalement administre un an post-TCC afin d'evaluer l'impact des sequelles cognitives sur leur qualite de vie. Le score total et les sous-scores a l'EXACT-P seront compares entre les differents groupes de patients (leger, modere et severe) par une MANOVA et la qualite de vie des jeunes sera examinee avec une regression.

column36: Development of an early warning system for progression in non-muscle invasive bladder cancer patients using time-series forecasting with artificial intelligence
column37: Bladder cancer is the 5th most common cancer in Canada with about 75% of these patients being diagnosed with non-muscle invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC), in which the tumour does not infiltrate the muscle layer surrounding the bladder. NMIBC has about a 65% recurrence rate but unfortunately, up to 20% of NMIBC patients will progress to more advanced stages of disease. While NMIBC can be managed with minimally invasive surgeries to remove bladder tumours or instilling medication into the bladder, higher stages such as muscle invasive bladder cancer requires extensive surgery which includes the removal of the bladder, nearby organs, and the need to create a urinary diversion to allow urine to drain from the kidneys to outside the body.As progression often occurs after multiple NMIBC recurrences, identifying patients at risk of progression is important for both patient counselling and clinical decision-making to guide frequency of follow-ups and the need for more aggressive upfront treatment. Unfortunately, current predictive models are limited due to poor performance and several practical issues. First, these models do not reflect the current standard of care for management of NMIBC, which includes re-resection of the tumour bed when indicated and use of intravesical therapies. Second, these models are time-fixed in that they do not capture changes in the patient's cancer status after initial diagnosis, which includes subsequent follow-ups and tumour recurrences. To address these shortcomings, we plan to develop a time-series forecasting model using artificial intelligence to better encapsulate the complete oncological timeline of contemporarily treated NMIBC patients to improve prognostic accuracy.

column36: Effects of Cannabinoid Compounds in a Dopamine Deficient Mouse Parkinson's Model
column37: Parkinsons disease is a neurological disorder that results in tremor, postural instability, and difficulty coordinating movement, like walking. Dopamine, an important neurotransmitter involved in motor control, is affected in Parkinsons disease. As dopaminergic neurons degenerate, symptoms of Parkinsons emerge. The standard drug treatment for Parkinsons is the use of L-DOPA, the precursor of dopamine. Unfortunately, prolonged use and high doses of L-DOPA are associated with a condition known as L-DOPA Induced Dyskinesia. Treatments that enhance L-DOPA and reduce the dose required for therapeutic effect are highly desired as they can delay the development of L-DOPA Induced Dyskinesia. The endocannabinoid system contains anandamide (AEA) and 2-arachidonoylglycerol (2-AG), which are endogenous ligands that primarily bind to cannabinoid receptors CB1 in the nervous system. Monoacylglycerol lipase (MAGL) is the enzyme which breaks down 2-AG. Preliminary studies from our lab have shown that the inhibition of MAGL can increase motor activity in mice. In this project, we aim to study the effect of endocannabinoid inhibitors (MAGL inhibition) and cannabinoids including tetrahydrocannabinol (THC), cannabidiol (CBD), and allosteric modulators of CB1 receptors, on enhancing the effects of L-DOPA in an acute mouse model of Parkinsons disease. Our Dopamine Transporter Dopamine Deficient mice (DDD) model has been successfully used to demonstrate the beneficial effects of amphetamine like compounds on enhancing L-DOPA activity. Our main hypothesis is that drug treatments that would increase L-DOPA efficacy or duration in our model would be beneficial for therapeutic intervention in Parkinsons and could potentially reduce or delay the development of L-DOPA Induced Dyskinesia.

column36: Master's Research Investigating Mouse Trophoblast Stem Cells in the Context of Placental Pathology
column37: The placenta is a pregnancy-specific organ that facilitates the exchange of oxygen, carbon dioxide, nutrients, and wastes between the mother and fetus (3). The cells that make up the placenta are called trophoblasts, and all trophoblasts are derived from trophoblast stem (TS) cells (3). Previously TS cells were believed to not be present beyond mid-gestation; however, recent evidence has shown that they may persist into mid-late mouse gestation and seem to increase in response to stress in mouse models of placental insufficiency, however, it is unknown whether they may help the placenta to adapt (4,5). This study will address that gap in knowledge by using a transgenic Eomes mouse, lineage tracing and a surgical model of preeclampsia that results in compromised placental development to investigate the response of persistent TS cells in placental pathology (4). Specifically, this study will characterize across gestation their ability to differentiate once removed from the mouse placenta and determine in response to placental stress whether their recruitment results in the contribution of differentiated trophoblast to the placenta. Further in vitro analysis will correlate epigenetic and differentiation profiles of isolated TS cells to determine whether they are altered in the compromised placentae. Once the response of TS cells in the context of placental pathology has been characterized, future studies will investigate whether these responses are helpful (adaptive) or harmful (pathological) to the placenta.

column36: Single-blind Randomized Control Trial of Prenatal Air Pollution Exposure and the Development of Wheeze in Children
column37: Air pollution is among the leading risk factors contributing to mortality around the world. Even relatively low levels of air pollution have been shown to increase respiratory symptoms and morbidities in children. In addition, increasing evidence suggests that the earliest impacts of air pollution occur before birth and that prenatal exposure impacts the developing fetus and increases the risk of morbidities over the entire life course. However, research on the developmental effects of air pollution exposure on respiratory development remains limited. Previous observational studies have failed to accurately assess prenatal exposures and account for residual confounding. Additionally, no studies have tested widely available interventions during pregnancy to improve respiratory health in young children. This study will assess the impact of prenatal air pollution exposure on the development of wheeze in early childhood and the effectiveness of portable air filters (;HEPA cleaners) in reducing those impacts in Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia, one of the worlds most polluted cities. This study design addresses previous studies limitations while moving beyond the identification of health risks and testing the efficacy of a widely available intervention. If HEPA cleaners are effective at reducing the developmental impacts of air pollution on wheeze, this work could produce knowledge that will improve the health of young children around the world.

column36: Epidemiological analysis of prenatal stress as a risk factor for the development of attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD)
column37: Attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is the most common mental disorder in children worldwide and can have lifelong health impacts, making it a major public health issue. Rates of ADHD have been increasing in Canada in recent years, particularly in Quebec, and increasing attention has been given to this diagnosis around the world. Previous research suggests there is a significant gender gap in ADHD in children, with boys much more likely to be diagnosed than girls. However, reasons for this difference remain largely unknown. Genetic factors are known to play a key role in the development of ADHD. Yet, genes do not act in isolation. The early environment can also strongly influence brain development and may modify the risk of ADHD. Specifically, maternal stress may alter the prenatal environment to increase the risk of developing ADHD, which may be more likely to impact males due to genetic sex differences. The proposed research will analyze the relationship between prenatal maternal stress, offspring sex, and genes in relation to the risk of later ADHD. I will carry out this analysis in four large independent prenatal cohorts from Canada, the UK, the Netherlands, and Singapore. Through the use of international, longitudinal data, the proposed project will be able to unpack the complex mechanisms that can result in the development of ADHD across different cohorts and settings. This will lead to a better understanding of the relevant genetic and environmental determinants of ADHD, to allow for better treatment options, and to identify potential areas of early intervention.

column37: In 2018, Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma (HNSCC) was the 6th most common cancer worldwide with approximately 890 000 new cases and 450 000 deaths. The burden of HNSCC is expected to rise by 30% by the year 2030. Amidst the advent of new therapeutic modalities in the past 10 years, the five-year survival rate still sits at roughly 50%. Improvement outcomes are desperately needed to help improve the overall survival and quality of life of patients.The molecular mechanisms behind HNSCC treatment resistance are not fully understood. However, due to advances in genomics, scientists now know about resistance mechanisms found in solid tumours. However, few studies have systemically assessed these mechanisms using a wide variety of human HNSCC tumours.Using the most recent advances in genomic technology, my research will focus on identifying altered molecular pathways involved in HNSCC treatment resistance by using a mouse model. Two treatment groups (control/cisplatin) will be used to identify the topmost treatment resistant and treatment sensitive patient tumours. I will then identify specific resistance patterns by comparing gene expression profiles between treatment resistant/sensitive patient tumours.HNSCC treatment resistance is a twofold problem. Current treatment options provide poor five-year survival rates and also profoundly alter the quality of life of patients. Long-term consequences include difficulty swallowing, speech and breathing impairment, hearing loss, risk of infections, etc. A systematic assessment of these molecular mechanisms could help us either identify future therapeutic targets or help us develop safer and more effective treatment options for the treatment of HNSCC.

column36: Trends in risk factors for diabetes in Canada: migration, temporal, and socioeconomic factors
column37: Knowledge of the diabetes risk factors and their trends has not been developed in Canada, making it difficult to assess the impact of prevention programs on the Canadian population. Differences in the prevalence of diabetes and associated risk factors have been noted across ethnic groups both within and between countries. With the growing diversity in Canada, a greater understanding of health status and risk factors prevalent in different population groups is important to guide culturally appropriate health interventions. In this study, we will examine national trends in diabetes and its risk factors from 2001 to 2018. The Canadian Community Health Survey will be combined from 2001-2018, which is a comprehensive national health survey of Canadas population aged 12 and up. The following risk factors will be examined: obesity, diet, physical activity, smoking, and hypertension. The risk factors evaluated can be prevented by changes in daily life and in health policy. We will also compare the differential trends between Canada born and immigrant populations, adjusting for age, sex, education status, socioeconomic, and migration factors. We expect to advance national understanding of differential exposures of diabetes risk factors and their trends related to geographic and sociodemographic factors.Monitoring trends and disparities in diabetes risk factors will provide benchmarks for future health strategies and address multilevel risk factors faced by immigrants and subsequently reduce disease burden.

column36: Is brain insulin resistance a feature of the biology of depression? A pilot multi-modality neuroimaging study in adolescents
column37: I will examine whether brain insulin resistance is involved in the pathophysiology of major depressive disorder (MDD). This research question evolved following the observation that MDD is often co-morbid with metabolic dysfunction such as weight gain and type 2 diabetes (T2D), and that insulin resistance is associated with greater depressive symptom severity and worse cognition. To explore this bidirectional relationship, 12 medication-naïve/free MDD patients aged 14 to 18 years old, and 12 age-, sex-, and weight-matched healthy controls, will participate in a single-blind crossover magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) study. This will include completing fasting blood work and two MRI sessions: the first following intranasal placebo, and after a short break, the second following intranasal insulin challenge (80 IU). The MRI sessions will measure insulin induced changes in connectivity, blood flow, and glutamate levels within brain regions of interest using resting state functional MRI, arterial spin labeling, and magnetic resonance spectroscopy, respectively. A brief cognitive assessment and an abdominal surface coil scan will also be performed to measure visceral and hepatic adiposity to identify the relationship between brain insulin resistance and these outcomes. It is hypothesized that brain insulin resistance will be higher in MDD participants compared to the healthy controls, and will also be associated with greater illness severity, worse cognitive performance, and greater hepatic and visceral adiposity. Demonstrating disrupted brain insulin action can provide novel insights into poorly understood mechanisms underlying the relationship between MDD and T2D, and help uncover modifiable risk factors that can be targeted at the earliest stages of the illness.

column36: Elucidating the disease-modifying mechanisms of delta-9-tetrahydrocannabinol in osteoarthritis
column37: Knee osteoarthritis (OA) affects approximately 250 million people worldwide. It alters the whole joint structure, including the synovium that facilitates joint lubrication and the cartilage required for smooth joint mobility. Severe chronic pain and disability commonly result from joint degeneration, creating a need for effective OA therapies. Cannabis is considered a potential therapeutic for those with OA because of its analgesic and anti-inflammatory properties. However, insufficient research has been done on its disease-modifying effects, leaving physicians unable to adequately guide patients on the appropriate use of cannabis products for treating OA. Cannabis is comprised of more than 100 active cannabinoid molecules, including delta-9-tetrahydrocannabinol (THC), that can alter the activity of receptive cells in the body. Joint cartilage and synovial cells express cannabinoid receptors that allow them to interact with THC; however, its effects on the local OA joint remain unknown. I hypothesize that THC modifies OA disease progression by influencing survival, inflammation, and optimal function of joint cells and tissues. To elucidate its mechanisms of action, I will treat human OA cartilage and synovial cells with THC and identify the relevant genes and proteins that are regulated. I will also use histological techniques to identify the effects of THC on OA joint cell states (like cell death, growth/spreading, and activation), immune cell invasion, and cartilage breakdown in knee joints from mice with OA-like features given oral THC treatment. Results from this proposed study may reveal novel signaling pathways of THC in the OA joint and help to inform scientists and clinicians of the potential use of cannabinoids for treating OA.

column36: Integration of Precision Medicine for Improving Management of Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD)
column37: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is a chronic lung condition characterised by obstructed airflow from the lungs that makes it difficult to breathe. COPD affects the lives of 2.6 million Canadians and is punctuated by an acute worsening of symptoms referred to as exacerbations which considerably deteriorates quality of life. It is already the leading cause of medical hospitalizations in Canada but its burden on our healthcare system continues to increase given the clear gaps in care. Clinical prediction tools can be used to accurately predict a patients risk of experiencing an exacerbation using their own health data which enables the personalisation of care to reduce the likelihood of future exacerbations. Despite the promises, clinical prediction tools are not routinely used in COPD and current management fails to consider the important individual differences between patients. My research will examine a new prediction tool developed to address this gap in care, the ACute COPD Exacerbation Prediction Tool (ACCEPT). Specifically, I will ensure that ACCEPT is up to date with contemporary Canadian clinical data by updating it using data from five major COPD research trials and compare ACCEPT against competing risk prediction methods in terms of their potential usefulness in a real-world clinical setting. Additionally, I will also develop a patient-friendly risk communication tool to facilitate shared decision-making. My research will inform an upcoming clinical trial to evaluate the impact of incorporating exacerbation risk prediction with ACCEPT into routine COPD care in British Columbia. This is a critical component of integrating clinical prediction tools into the routine management of COPD and has real possibility to improve patient care and outcomes.

column36: Investigating the validity of accelerometer-based measures of physical activity and sedentary time in toddlers (iPLAY)
column37: Physical activity can impact how a child grows and develops from a very young age. It can also change how healthy they are. It is important to know exactly how much time a child spends being active or inactive. That way if theyre not getting enough activity, we can help them to move more. One way to measure physical activity is using accelerometers. In older children, accelerometers can help us monitor exactly how much time they spend doing really easy activities and activities that get their hearts pumping. Yet, very little research uses accelerometers with toddlers, or children between the ages of 12 to 35 months. The goal of my research on the iPLAY study is to figure out if and how we can use accelerometers to measure physical activity in toddlers. To do this, we video recorded toddlers doing different activities while wearing an accelerometer. I will compare each second of the video to the accelerometer and see how well they match. By figuring this out, we can create instructions for other researchers who are also measuring physical activity in young children. It will help us better understand how much toddlers move. This is important because once we can measure how active they are, we can study how much activity can help to make sure toddlers are growing up as healthy as possible.

column36: Novel CTRP8-DLK1 interaction alters NOTCH1 signaling to support tumor stem cells
column37: A network of different cell types within a tumor, such as cancer stem cells and immune cells, regulates tumor growth and survival. Current drugs are ineffective in the targeted disruption of cancer stem cells, which enables these cells to retain their potential to initiate tumor growth. Immune cells can infiltrate tumors and create an environment that supresses or supports cancer cell survival. In our studies, we have identified that the protein C1q-TNF related protein 8 (CTRP8) is present in immune cell populations of brain, breast, lung and prostate cancer tissue. We have also observed that immune cells that support aggressive tumor growth produce higher levels of CTRP8. Much remains unknown about the function of CTRP8, but our recent findings have identified CTRP8 as a promising new link between the immune system and cancer biology.We have previously found that presence of CTRP8 in the brain tumor glioblastoma causes cancer cells to invade surrounding tissue and become resistant to treatment drugs. In our ongoing investigation of the roles of CTPR8 in cancer, we discovered a new interaction that occurs between CTRP8 and Delta-like homolog protein 1 (DLK1). In many cancers, including brain tumors, DLK1 keeps tumor cells in a cancer stem-cell like state. The new CTRP8 and DLK1 interaction will highlight new functional immune-tumor cell networks and their impact on the cancer stem cell population of tumors.

column36: Improving antidepressant treatment in the postpartum by manipulating immune signalling: impact on dam and offspring
column37: During periods of hormone shifts such as the postpartum period, females experience a heightened risk for depression. Antidepressants such as selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIS) are beneficial in improving depression symptoms. However, these benefits are rarely seen in women experiencing Postpartum depression (PPD). Children of mothers with PPD show an increased risk of psychiatric disorders. Thus, there is an urgent need to develop better therapies to treat PPD. Current research suggests that this increased risk may be related to inflammatory markers which may also be implicated in antidepressant efficacy. Specifically, the major immune cells in the brain, microglia secrete immune signalling factors called cytokines, such as Interleukin (IL)-1b. IL-1b and microglia are implicated in PPD, SSRI efficacy, and are highly expressed in the hippocampus during depression. Reduced neuroplasticity in the hippocampus is seen in PPD, and IL-1b suppresses hippocampal neuroplasticity. To determine the involvement of IL-1b and microglia in SSRI efficacy in PPD we will administer a drug that reduces the effects of IL-1b along with SSRI treatment in a rodent model of PPD, and measure depressive-like symptoms. We will examine the effects maternal treatments in male and female offspring, particularly stress resilience during adolescence, as this is the time when disorders in children of PPD mothers often emerge. We hypothesize that blocking IL-1b will boost SSRI efficacy and alleviate depressive-like symptoms in the dam and stress resilience in offspring. This project will study the mechanism underlying decreased antidepressant efficacy seen in PPD and may promote viable targets to be used for treatment of PPD, that will benefit the health of both mother and child alike.
